params.name: S1.1
params.hypothesis: Connected horizontal-stroke detector: It responds along connected strokes, horizontal ones most: the three arms of a 3 and the top, waist and bottom of an 8. The same ink scattered as separate pixels gives it little, which is why shuffled-pixel noise leaves it lowest and 3s raise it most. So moving a 3's or 8's own ink pixels to random places in its box should lower it far more than mirroring the box, and a horizontal stroke should raise it more than the same stroke upright. Self-probe: On 3s and 8s, the digit's ink pixels moved to random places in its box vs the box mirrored left to right: -1.50 SD against the control (95% interval -1.54 to -1.46, 667 images; predicted down): agrees. A 10-pixel horizontal stroke through the centre of the image's ink vs the same stroke upright: +0.39 SD against the control (95% interval +0.37 to +0.42, 1000 images; predicted up): agrees. Behaviour (the conclusion): It fires on most 3s (89%) and rarely on noise images (10%). Within each class, the larger the amount of horizontal-stroke edge, the stronger the response (Spearman r = +0.58 averaged over classes; partial r = +0.46 with the class and the ink count held fixed). Concept check: Named concepts that also hold within classes, with the ink held fixed: tall stem (less: fires on 43% of images with it vs 73% without, same class); wide (more: fires on 80% of images with it vs 58% without, same class). So an upright stroke along the left edge should raise it far more than the same stroke along the right edge or the same stroke lying horizontal at the left edge; mirroring a 3 left to right (its closed side then on the left) should raise it; and moving the whole image content 4 pixels left instead of right should change nothing. The image content moved 4 pixels left vs 4 pixels right: +0.01 SD against the control (95% interval -0.00 to +0.02, 1000 images; predicted no change): agrees. Behaviour (the conclusion): It fires on most 8s (98%) and rarely on 3s (3%). Within each class, the larger the upright-stroke edge in the left half of the ink's box, the stronger the response (Spearman r = +0.34 averaged over classes; partial r = +0.28 with the class and the ink count held fixed). On 8s, erase the left third of the digit vs as many ink pixels from its right third (the '8' score margin): -1.48 SD against the control (95% interval -1.86 to -1.11, 110 images; predicted down): agrees. On noise images, a 10-pixel horizontal stroke along the top of the ink vs the same stroke upright there (the 'noise' score margin): -0.53 SD against the control (95% interval -0.64 to -0.42, 333 images; predicted down): agrees.
